page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The hardware layout consists of 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, providing 8 vCPUs. System memory is provisioned at 16.0 GB RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio (2.0 GB per core). The processor incorporates 35 MB of L3 cache alongside vector instruction support including AVX, AVX-512, and AVX512 VNNI. Network interconnects supply a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps, while local disk storage is absent.

Performance benchmark results place the multi-core processing capability in an average tier, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 4486.0 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 7001.83. Memory read bandwidth reaches 50.07 GB/sec for uncached blocks, supporting a static web serving throughput of 6.74 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 6.8 million operations per second. In contrast, single-core efficiency shows lower relative standing, marked by weak scores in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. The lack of built-in local SSD storage requires total reliance on attached network storage solutions for persistent data.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the resource configuration concentrates spending on CPU core density rather than memory or integrated disk hardware. This precise resource ratio reduces waste for workloads that do not require high memory capacity. The instance provides a balanced profile for multi-threaded, stateless compute applications, software compilation tasks, web server clusters, and distributed caching layers.
description: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture using a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Equipped with 35 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 extensions, it contains no local storage and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate average multi-core CPU, memory bandwidth, and database performance, including static web serving throughput of 6.74 GB/sec and 6.8 million Redis SET operations per second. Single-core compression tasks show lower relative performance. The lack of bundled local storage requires external network storage. This instance offers cost-effective CPU resource density tailored for multi-threaded stateless microservices, web serving, software compilation, and in-memory caching.
